_comment: Areas where an upstream change can break Typos even when it merges without a conflict. Matched against every path upstream changed. risk: high = stop and read before applying; medium = review; low = note. Edit this as the fork grows.

areas.note: Possibly a new Gecko (Firefox) version. Typos' Windows build downloads prebuilt Gecko components; a new version needs new components, the NSIS installer scripts re-checked, and the launcher/updater binaries re-fetched: upstream keeps those in Git LFS, which Typos does not copy (the upstream watch does not list them), so also compare upstream's app/win/zotero.exe.tar.xz and updater.exe.tar.xz pointer files (oid and size) with app/lfs-files.json and update that file. Check app/config.sh by hand.

Changes how the database is built or upgraded. Typos adds the Classic Work type on top (fork/schema/overlay.json, built by fork/scripts/build-schema.js). A schema or migration change can't be undone on users' libraries: after applying, run `node fork/scripts/build-schema.js --check`, test with a copy of a real library, and never run a new build against your only copy.
Item types, fields and relations. Typos' Classic Work type and relationships depend on these.
Where Typos adds its own modules and start-up calls (Zotero.Backup.init, Zotero.TyposUpdater.init, ...). A merge can silently drop or reorder them: check the module list and init calls afterwards.
Typos hooks abbreviation lists and per-document profiles into citation output here.

Build scripts, installer and dependencies. Typos' installer is renamed, supports per-user and all-users installs, and the build is driven from .github/workflows; upstream changes here need to be carried over by hand.
Typos adds menu items (Tools, Help), preferences and an item-pane section in these files.
Typos adds its own preferences, and keeps Mozilla's app.update.* switched off so the app can never be replaced by upstream's updater.
Strings. After applying, run `npm run rebrand` so new upstream strings say Typos.
Logos and icons were replaced with Typos' own. Don't let upstream artwork come back.
Pointers to other repositories (translators, styles, PDF reader, note editor, ...). Updating one is a separate step: `git submodule update --remote <path>` in a branch.
